jobs.description:
People With Disabilities Foundation (PWDF) is seeking a Deputy Executive Director (DED).


PWDF is a small nonprofit agency in San Francisco that provides education and advocacy for people with psychiatric and/or developmental disabilities so they can achieve equal opportunities in all aspects of life. Applicants should look at website (www.pwdf.org) before applying in order to understand the scope of our work and submit a more meaningful cover letter. This is an on\-site position.


Compensation: $78,000 – $82,000 annual base range for fulltime (35 hours per week), depending on experience, plus benefits. Benefits include medical and dental insurance, vacation, and Commuter Checks according to agency policy, effective after 90 days, and holidays.


POSITION DESCRIPTION: The position is to assist the Executive Director (ED). The DED reports to the ED.


Duties: Under the supervision of the ED, the DED is to be able to perform all ED duties:


(1\) Hiring, onboarding, and staff support for PWDF, including all HR issues.


(2\) Oversee and support Director of Public Awareness/Education and Office Manager. Support the Advocacy Program and its support staff (two to three).


(3\) Oversee PWDF’s Pilot Grant program.


(4\) Monitor income and expenses with bookkeeper; prepare reports as needed. Coordinate with bookkeeper and resolve problems related to payroll, bookkeeping, and tax return.


(5\) Administer contracts for vendors, including insurance policies. Handle problems if any, with bookkeeper, payroll, computers and other office equipment, office lease, and other issues that arise.


(6\) Ensure compliance with all state and local laws and reporting requirements, e.g., California Workplace Violence Prevention Plan, San Francisco ARF, respectively.


(6\) Provide support and oversee IT vendors for computers and other office equipment.


(7\) Prepare reports for PWDF Board of Directors.


(8\) General development including locating and networking with supportive partners and monitoring of same. Communications, coordination and cooperation with other public or non\-profit agencies serving our target population.


(9\) Must be able to attend and fulfill duties for occasional liaison meetings, which may be called without due notice.


(10\) Other duties as requested.


Qualifications:


Required:  

1\. Licensed California Attorney, JD, Ph.D., or equivalent and minimum 8\-10 years of relevant; e.g., civil rights nonprofit, experience.  

2\. Exceptional communication skills (oral and written); ability to write clearly including accuracy for detail with data in spreadsheets and other formats.


Highly Preferred; demonstrated transferrable skills helpful:  

1\. Experience in Social Security, employment, health care and other disability rights in both advocacy and education. Legal background helpful.  

2\. General knowledge of disability civil rights and Social Security/SSI disability necessary to administratively oversee PWDF’s programs or equivalent experience.  

3\. Knowledge of GAAP and bookkeeping, IT skills, employment laws and HR skills, working with and resolving vendor disputes, and nonprofit tax return filing (we have a CPA).


This is at a non\-profit organization. PWDF is an EEO and Fair Chance Employer. Principals only. Recruiters please do not contact this job poster.


To apply: Submit a cover letter that states why you want to work at PWDF, resume, and writing sample not edited by another source to info@pwdf.org. No calls please.

**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Location:** Los Angeles, CA

**Job Type:** Full\-Time, hybrid

**About LocoL**

Alta Community (dba LocoL) is a nonprofit in Watts, which provides culinary job training and education for young people while addressing food insecurity through the preparation and distribution of affordable, high\-quality meals, primarily for local nonprofits. Founded as a nonprofit in 2023 by chefs Keith Corbin and Daniel Patterson, LocoL is on the site of the former LocoL restaurant, originally founded by chefs Roy Choi and Daniel Patterson.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and has overall authority and accountability for organizational strategy, personnel, operations, programs, fundraising, and financial management, within policies and budgets approved by the Board.

The Executive Director will lead Alta Community/LocoL through its next stage of organizational development, strengthening the systems, partnerships, revenue, team, and strategy required to deliver sustainable community impact. The Executive Director will have overall responsibility for organizational leadership, fundraising and earned\-revenue growth, financial stewardship, program quality and impact, team development, and external relationships.

This is an opportunity for a hands\-on, entrepreneurial leader who can move comfortably between long\-term strategy and practical execution. The successful candidate will understand how to build an emerging nonprofit organization while respecting LocoL’s history, community relationships, culinary identity, and commitment to economic opportunity and food justice.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Strategy \& Administration**

* In partnership with the board of directors, develop and execute a strategic plan for the next five years of growth and impact.
* Ensure operational and programmatic alignment with the organization’s values and goals.
* Engage the Board through quarterly meetings to facilitate effective org governance.
* Improve and implement HR practices for employee success, including performance management, compensation and staffing, and employee development and retention.
* Build and develop a high\-performing, inclusive team, ensuring role clarity and fostering a culture of growth, accountability, and teamwork.
* Ensure compliance with California employment requirements.

**Fundraising, Communications \& Financial Management**

* Develop and implement a revenue strategy including earned income meal contracts, grants, and individual giving to raise and sustainably expand \~$700K operating budget.
* Build and maintain relationships with donors, foundations, and funding partners.
* Strengthen partnerships with nonprofits, community leaders and hiring partners.
* Leverage data to enhance organizational storytelling and external communications to grow awareness, convey impact to key stakeholders, and drive fundraising targets.
* Oversee financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for fiscal sustainability, including cash\-flow management, financial controls, monthly financial reporting and forecasting, grant reporting, insurance and risk management and earned income margins.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate tax and accounting standards, as well as nonprofit regulations, reporting, and best practices.
* Oversee planning of fundraising and community events, as needed.

**Program Development**

Recruit and manage a new Program Manager to ensure organizational alignment and effective program delivery. Program Manager responsibilities include:

* Manage six program staff members and develop a hiring plan to fill additional capacity needs within the organization.
* Expand and refine programs that provide culinary training, cooking education, and affordable catering for nonprofits.
* Ensure operational success for LocoL, including kitchen operations, quality control, menu development, budgets, vendor relationships and customer service.
* Collaborate with chef leaders at LocoL to develop and implement a job training program, focusing on culinary skills, hospitality, and professional development.
* Mentor and coach team members, many of whom are entering the workforce for the first time, to help them achieve their full potential.
* Oversee outcome measurement to demonstrate effectiveness.

**Required capabilities**

* Passion for community and workforce development, food justice, and economic empowerment.
* Proven executive or senior leadership in nonprofit management, social enterprises, or related fields.
* Experience partnering with board of directors and leading teams.
* Strong track record in fundraising, grants, and financial management.
* Excellent strategic thinking, communication, storytelling, and advocacy skills.

**Strongly preferred capabilities**

* Social\-enterprise leadership.
* Food, culinary, hospitality, catering, or production experience.
* Los Angeles or Watts community relationships.
* Early\-stage organizational building.
* Brand and communications experience.
* Government contracting or institutional meal contracts.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

* Salary Range: $90,000\-$110,000 (commensurate with experience).
* Stipend for healthcare.
* Paid\-time off and paid sick time.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to **info@altacommunityla.org** with the subject line **“Executive Director Application – LocoL.”** Priority will be given to applications received by August 31, 2026\.

**About Back on My Feet**


Back on My Feet is a national nonprofit that uses the power of running and community to help people experiencing homelessness and addiction transform their lives. Operating across 14 markets, we meet members where they are — before sunrise, on the road, in community — and challenge them to do something hard together. That challenge is where transformation begins. Since our founding, we have believed that when you change how someone sees themselves, you change what they believe is possible. Running is how we start. The rest follows.

**Our Strategic Anchors**


Everything we do is guided by four anchors. They are not aspirational — they are operational.

**We Drive Real Impact —** We measure success by transformation, not activity. *The Executive Director is the local owner of that standard. Every program decision, every partner conversation, every day\-to\-day call must be traceable to one question: are we creating transformation that* *wouldn't* *happen without us?*

**Running Is Our Foundation —** Running is not a feature of our program. It is the mechanism through which transformation begins. *The Executive Director* *is responsible for* *ensuring running stays structurally central to local delivery — not as a requirement on paper, but as a living, daily practice that members, volunteers, and staff experience as real.*

**We Build Local Roots for Lasting Impact —** Real transformation happens in communities, not across them. *The Executive Director is the face of* *BoMF* *in their chapter: embedded, trusted, and accountable. The chapter should feel like* *BoMF. It should also feel* *like* *home.*

**Our People Are the Movement —** Back on My Feet runs on people. *The Executive Director* *is responsible for* *the humans who make this possible in their chapter: members, alumni, volunteers, and local staff — ensuring they are supported, developed, and connected to something larger than any single chapter.*

 **The Positio**n


The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for leading the local chapter to achieve program objectives, fundraising targets, and managing and growing the annual local budget in alignment with Back on My Feet's Four Strategic Anchors: *We Drive Real Impact, Running Is Our Foundation, We Build Local Roots for Lasting Impact,* and *Our People Are the Movement*. This role oversees a team of local staff, manages the stewardship of the local Advisory Board, and operates within a matrix structure: reporting to the VP of Program through their Territory Director for mission and delivery, and to the Partnerships team for revenue.

  

The Executive Director is the operational leader of their chapter. They own day\-to\-day program delivery, local fundraising and development, partner and volunteer relationships, and team performance. They are not managers waiting for direction. They are a local owner, accountable for the full P\&L and mission outcomes of their chapter.

 **Key Responsibilities**

**Program Strategy, Implementation \& Delivery**

* Own and drive local implementation of the BoMF program model, ensuring running is structurally central to all member touchpoints, from Circle Ups (BOMF’s community based running practice) to workforce development.
* Strengthen and expand BoMF's local presence by cultivating new facility partnerships and deepening engagement with existing partners, ensuring sustained growth in program KPIs.
* Oversee delivery of BoMF's workforce development program; grow and strengthen partnerships with referral agencies, corporate partners, and employment partners to provide members with needed support and services.
* Ensure program model fidelity. If running culture drifts, energy erodes, or standards slip, the ED owns the identification and correction of that drift at the local level, in coordination with the VP of Program and Chief Running Officer.
* Source and share member stories, outcomes, and program data with national teams on a defined cadence to support organizational reporting, marketing, and donor engagement.

**Leadership \& Staff Management**

* Hire, manage, and develop local staff, fostering a collaborative, high\-performing environment grounded in BoMF's Strategic Anchors.
* Set clear expectations, provide ongoing feedback, and hold staff accountable to program and operational KPIs.
* Build a local team culture where running, community, and transformation are not talking points, they are operating principles.
* Collaborate with Program leadership on annual goals, performance reviews, and professional development for local staff.

**Volunteer Engagement \& Management**

* Manage and grow a robust volunteer community to support chapter goals and initiatives, ensuring volunteers have a shared understanding of BoMF's mission and adhere to BoMF policies and procedures.
* Recruit, train, and retain individual and corporate volunteers to support Circle Ups, workforce development, events, and fundraising goals.
* Ensure volunteers receive consistent, timely, and mission\-aligned communications about program activities, expectations, and culture.

**Fundraising \& Donor Relations**

* Develop and execute an overall local fundraising strategy to meet or exceed annual fundraising targets and chapter budget goals, carrying primary P\&L responsibility for the chapter.
* Cultivate and steward relationships with local donors, corporate partners, and foundations.
* Identify and secure diverse local funding sources, including grants, individual donors, and corporate sponsorships.
* Plan and manage local fundraising events to generate revenue and community awareness, in coordination with the national Partnerships Team.
* Collaborate with the Partnerships Team on national partnerships, relationships, and campaigns; ensure neither function commits the other without prior alignment.
* Build, engage, and grow the local Advisory Board to advance fundraising, partnerships, and program objectives.

**Three generations. Multiple plants. One operator to run them.**


Press\-Seal Corporation has been manufacturing specialty rubber sealing products for the waterworks and industrial markets for three generations, family\-owned throughout. Our products sit underground in municipal infrastructure across North America, where failure is not an option and quality is not negotiable.


We are no longer a single\-plant company. Through acquisition and organic growth, we now operate multiple manufacturing facilities across Indiana, with more expected. We are creating the role of Chief Operating Officer to run them. Ownership will still be involved in plant\-level duties.

**Purpose of Position**


Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO owns manufacturing across all Press\-Seal facilities — Fort Wayne, Jasper, InSeal, and the plants we acquire next. You will carry the operating P\&L and be measured on three things above all: throughput, cost, and margin.


You will also own all of engineering — new product development and plant\-level industrial engineering both. That means one person is accountable for what we decide to build, how fast it gets to launch, and whether the process on the floor can actually make it at cost. Few operating roles at this size carry that whole span.


This is a floor role, not a corner office. You will know the extrusion lines, presses, mixers, lathe\-cut cells, and the people running them. You will decide which work belongs at which plant, where the constraints are, and what capital is worth spending. When we buy a company, you are the one who makes the operating thesis real.

**What You’ll Own**

* Consolidated operating P\&L across all manufacturing sites
* All engineering — new product development and plant\-level industrial engineering
* Plant leadership development and accountability
* Capacity, capital planning, and constraint removal
* Quality systems (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, PPAP, NSF 61\) and EHS performance
* Materials strategy, inventory, and supply resilience
* Operating integration of acquired facilities

**What We’re Looking For**

* A decade or more of manufacturing leadership with multi\-site P\&L ownership — you have run more than one plant at the same time
* Experience leading engineering on both sides: product development timelines and plant\-level industrial engineering
* A track record integrating acquisitions or turning around underperforming operations
* Materials\-processing background: rubber, polymer, plastics, or similar — mixing, molding, or extrusion
* Real fluency in lean methods and formal quality systems
* A results record you can put numbers to


Rubber compounding or molding depth, and experience in waterworks, filtration, or tier automotive supply, will move you to the top of the list.

**Why Press\-Seal**


We are family\-owned and intend to stay that way. That means decisions get made in days, not quarters, and the person setting strategy is in the building. It also means we take a long view — we are building an operating platform, not dressing up a company for sale.


You will report to the CEO with a direct line, a real mandate, and the authority to match it.

jobs.description:
**Director Of Operations**

*Our mantra is simple \- love. Love what you do. Love where you live. Love the success and return we provide. At RR Living, we are a part of something special.*


The Director of Operations is a key leadership position responsible for growing a team of people who will effectively execute the company’s business strategy. Operational leaders are empowered to drive the financial success of multi\-million\-dollar communities and assets within a defined portfolio/region while providing strategic leadership, management oversight and accountability for several areas of performance including property operations, portfolio financial results, compliance, talent acquisition, team member development, customer and resident satisfaction, asset preservation, service, facilities \& expense control. You ensure that established business strategy and financial performance targets are achieved or exceeded.


**Responsibilities**

* You and your community teams are expected to drive operational improvement including increasing physical and economic occupancy at the communities assigned to you. This will be accomplished through hiring and developing a stable well\-trained team of professionals who understand the RR Living Core Values and drive excellence at the community and with resident satisfaction.
* You are expected to achieve Budgeted Income, Expenses and CNOI every month, quarter, and year on the assets you are responsible for.
* Proactively recognize trends and market conditions that may impact property performance. Become an expert on the markets you are in, know your competition and how those communities align with our community.
* Using strategy and experience, successfully lead through economic downturns to ensure the assets under your direction are leading the market in performance and proforma budget achievement.
* Achieve and maintain delinquency at less than 2% on stabilized assets. On assigned assets above 2%, goal percentages will be developed during your first 30 days of employment, to outline tiered expectations to ultimately achieve the 2% or better goal on each asset within 90 days.
* Achieve portfolio and proforma occupancy goals and maintaining a 95% or above occupancy
* Grow rental rate and income in accordance with ownership business strategies and assigned budget, and at a minimum striving to achieve 2% more than market average.
* Build a team of direct reports and community team members that understand the importance of executing an exemplary resident experience, receiving excellent and respectful service every day.
* Ensure your portfolio pays attention to the details, including curb appeal, a safe and enjoyable community atmosphere, well maintained amenities, and rental homes where residents are proud to have family and friends visit.
* Ensure communities are well\-maintained physically, including make\-readies, preventive maintenance, and the completion of service requests within 48 hours of submission.
* Ensure communities in your portfolio achieve net move\-in goals, retention and rate expectations and administrative reporting that is on time and accurate.
* Hire, train, mentor and develop future leaders and community team members. Proactively manage underperformers by training them, developing them and respectfully off boarding those who are not performing.
* Frequently conduct physical property walks, including the inspection of all grounds, community spaces such as hallways, breezeways, vacant apartment homes, clubhouses, shops, amenity areas, entrance and exit areas and community offices to ensure cleanliness, condition and that all areas are in good working order.
* Quickly learn how to navigate and use the computer software programs utilized by the company including Real Page One Site, On\-Site, AppFolio, Knock, Buzz, Apartment IQ Rentable, and more.
* Maintain ethical, professional, respectful, and courteous relationships with residents, teammates, and other customers. Follow all local, federal, and state regulations including Fair Housing Guidelines
* Act as an Ambassador of RR Living building relationships in the surrounding neighborhoods and community, and in our RR Giving Impact Initiatives.
* Ask questions, think strategically and lead your team with a Founder’s Mentality while being an integral and key part of the property management leadership team.

**RR Living's Core Values**

* **Be Your Best. Do Your Best.**

*We celebrate individualism, collaboration, and inclusion. Our associates are the best in the business, exemplifying that which we celebrate as an organization. Recognizing happiness and great attitudes are contagious, we hold ourselves and each other accountable. Success begets success and happiness begets happiness***.**




* **Honesty, Integrity, and an Unwavering Commitment to Excellence:**

*Excellent resident experiences are our specialty, recognizing the unique challenges of rentership. We provide a wonderful place to call Home, striving to do what is often missed \- creating unparalleled living experiences for our residents, incredible opportunities for our associates, and impressive revenues for our partners \&; owners.* ***Simply put, we Care.***




* **Empowered Associates, Obsessively Purpose\-Driven and Stronger Together:**

*Success, a people\-centric approach, and revenue growth are not independent of each other. We operate as one team. deliberate in the actions taken to drive revenue and improved valuation for owners \& investors. As happy performers, our associates are an engaged team empowered to work together to achieve our common goals, making us an unstoppable successful organization***.**




* **The Magic is in the Details:**

*Recognizing that residents choose to live where they can be proud of residing, we understand that details matter. Our teams provide personalized service that exceeds expectations and creates unique neighborhood\-like environments. From elite resident events to local partnerships

 **POSITION SUMMARY*****:***


Kentucky Wesleyan College seeks a collaborative, strategic, and relationship\-driven fundraising professional to serve as Senior Director of Development. This leadership position is responsible for expanding philanthropic support through the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major and planned gift donors.


The Senior Director manages a portfolio of approximately 100–150 major gift prospects and donors, developing personalized engagement strategies that inspire transformational philanthropy. Working in partnership with Advancement colleagues, academic leadership, faculty, alumni, volunteers, and community stakeholders, this position advances the College's mission by securing significant philanthropic investments that support institutional priorities and student success.


The successful candidate is an experienced frontline fundraiser who combines strong relationship\-building skills with strategic planning, data\-informed decision\-making, and a commitment to exceptional donor experiences. This position contributes to a culture of philanthropy through collaboration, innovation, accountability, and measurable fundraising outcomes.

* Conduct regular discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship visits with alumni, friends, parents, and community partners, utilizing data\-informed moves management practices.
* Develop individualized donor engagement and solicitation strategies that align donor interests with institutional funding priorities and increase philanthropic support.
* Build and maintain a healthy major gift pipeline through prospect research, qualification, tracking, forecasting, and collaboration with Advancement colleagues.
* Partner with faculty, staff, and campus leaders to create meaningful donor engagement opportunities and strengthen relationships across the College community.
* Lead and support donor stewardship and recognition efforts, ensuring donors are meaningfully engaged, acknowledged, and informed about the impact of their philanthropy.
* Collaborate with Advancement colleagues to develop compelling donor communications, promote institutional impact, and share alumni, student, and donor success stories.
* Assist in the planning and execution of donor cultivation, stewardship, recognition, and advancement events.
* Maintain accurate donor records, contact reports, and prospect activity within the College's constituent relationship management system.
* Serve as a strategic partner to Advancement leadership by contributing to fundraising strategy, revenue growth initiatives, and best practices in donor engagement.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Vice President for Advancement.

Bachelor’s degree; minimum of two years of experience in major gift fundraising preferably in an educational environment; a proven and verifiable track record of success in identifying, cultivating, and soliciting major gifts.

* Clear understanding of moves management in professional fundraising.
* Proven ability to successfully identify and build relationships with donors to connect their interests with opportunities in a higher education or other nonprofit organization.
* Basic understanding of planned gift concepts.
* A demonstrated ability to engage and effectively communicate with diverse audiences.
* Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to persuasively articulate institutional impact and funding needs.
* Strong work ethic, self\-awareness, and ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues across campus.
* Ability and willingness to travel, work occasional evenings and weekends, and participate in donor and institutional events as needed.
* Valid driver's license or ability to obtain reliable transportation for travel related to fundraising and constituent engagement activities.

 **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Ability to develop and execute fundraising plans with strong support of metrics.
* High level of creativity, initiative, and motivation.
* Demonstrated knowledge of all facets of fundraising, including annual fund, corporate and foundation relations, planned giving, stewardship, major gift fundraising, etc.
* Ability to work cross\-functionally with academic and administrative leaders in a collaborative environment to conceive and implement innovative ideas.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience working in a CRM or other relational database such as Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge.

Back on My Feet is a national nonprofit that uses the power of running and community to help people experiencing homelessness and addiction transform their lives. Running is how we start. The rest follows.

**Our Strategic Anchors**


Everything we do is guided by four anchors. They are not aspirational — they are operational.

**We Drive Real Impact —** We measure success by transformation, not activity. *The Executive Director is the local owner of that standard. Every program decision, every partner conversation, every day\-to\-day call must be traceable to one question: are we creating transformation that* *wouldn't* *happen without us?*

**Running Is Our Foundation —** Running is not a feature of our program. **We Build Local Roots for Lasting Impact —** Real transformation happens in communities, not across them. *The Executive Director is the face of* *BoMF* *in their chapter: embedded, trusted, and accountable. The chapter should feel like* *BoMF. It should also feel* *like* *home.*

**Our People Are the Movement —** Back on My Feet runs on people. *The Executive Director* *is responsible for* *the humans who make this possible in their chapter: members, alumni, volunteers, and local staff — ensuring they are supported, developed, and connected to something larger than any single chapter.*

**REPORTS** **TO:** Director of Advancement Communications
**ABOUT** **US:***The Advancement Team connects alumni and friends with Lawrence University’s mission by** *Investing in relationships,*
* *Matching donor and volunteer passions with university priorities, and*
* *Demonstrating the impact of philanthropy and volunteer engagement on our students and their Lawrence experience*

**PRIMARY****OBJECTIVE****:**
As the Assistant Director of Advancement Communications you will be responsible for the execution of a multi\-channel marketing and communications plan that contributes to the University’s alumni and donor engagement goals. Your work will capture and share the Lawrence story in engaging and broad\-reaching ways. This role will support fundraising priorities to support current and future students, steward donors, and engage our 20,000\+ alumni – all while contributing to the university’s visibility and reputation as a leading liberal arts institution.**KEY****RESPONSIBILITIES****:**
Support the Advancement division’s integrated marketing and communications efforts by contributing to alumni and donor engagement through compelling storytelling across multiple channels.* Execute email campaigns designed to drive annual fund support, event registration, and alumni affinity and connectedness.
* Manage and grow our social media presence and engagement across the Lawrence University Alumni Facebook page, LinkedIn group, and Instagram page — including developing a strategic social media content calendar and designing visually compelling posts using Canva.
* Support digital storytelling strategies with print mail campaigns, coordinating print projects through external vendors.
  



Serve as a primary resource with AlumnIQ, our email marketing platform, as well as ThankView, our donor stewardship email and video platform.* Serve as a campus consultant, training other platform users to increase platform and channel effectiveness.
* Stay updated on best practices.
* Collaborate in design, content, and managing distribution of emails.
* Ensure emails align with best practices for optimal performance and accessibility.
* Provide quality assurance of email marketing efforts to ensure best practices and engagement tracking for communications across the division.


Serve as a content contributor and coordinator for the alumni website. Assist in the creation and updating of microsites, special event sites, and other web products.
  

Assist with writing, content generation, and editing expertise for the Advancement division.
  

Support crowdfund initiatives with marketing and communications plans.
  

Maintain the Advancement division email and event calendar, ensuring open and collaborative communication and planning amongst the various stakeholders.
  

Maintain and respond to communications in the Alumni inbox with exemplary customer service and representing the University in a professional and compassionate manner.

Support Advancement and University events as requested or required.
  

Respond to special projects and other duties as assigned.
  

Some evening and weekend work is required.
**WORKING****RELATIONSHIPS****:**
The Assistant Director will work most closely with the Advancement Team, particularly the Alumni and Community Engagement team. Additionally, the Assistant Director will work with faculty, students, and staff across campus and the University’s constituents—alumni, donors, parents, friends, and Fox Valley community members.

The Assistant Director must establish and maintain positive working relationships with other key campus offices, such as Athletics, University Communications and Student Life, as well as off campus vendors for print solicitations and email marketing efforts.
**KNOWLEDGE****AND****SKILLS****:**
* Bachelor’s degree in related area with an appreciation for private, liberal arts, residential colleges.


* Two or more years relevant experience.


* Exceptional writing, communication, and editing skills, as well as accuracy and attention to detail.


* The ideal candidate will bring both copywriting and graphic design skills with the ability to create polished, on\-brand digital content for social media and email.


* Familiarity with at least one major email marketing system.


* Demonstrated experience formatting letters, designing webpages, and managing social media platforms – Facebook, LinkedIn, and Instagram at a minimum.


* Solution oriented with a demonstrated ability to problem\-solve.


* Demonstrated success in a fast\-moving, multi\-stakeholder environment, balancing multiple projects and priorities.


* Collaborative team player with a proactive attitude.


* Creativity, willingness to learn, and a sense of humor.


* Possess exceptional interpersonal and customer service skills i.e., concise, articulate, and confident with the ability to represent the university in a professional manner.


* Ability to maintain confidentiality of all aspects of job responsibilities.


**EMPLOYMENT****REQUIREMENTS****:**
Must have successful completion of criminal record check, driving record check (where applicable) and reference checks.
